text:
customer-sre: Hey team — since the failover policy change last night ~00:45 UTC a subset of our traffic is consistently routed to eu-central-1 even though our app is in us-west-2. Latency jumped from ~60ms to ~320ms and our bill spiked. Any quick checks we should run?

maria_support: sorry about that — can you paste the org id and a sample request id / curl so we can trace?

customer-sre: org: org-12345. example request id: req_0a1b2c3d. quick repro (from our app host in us-west):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Client-Id: app-abc" -H "X-Prefer-Region: us-west-2" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

response headers show: X-Served-Region: eu-central-1

infra-bot: deploy-bot: updated failover-policy for org-12345 by devops_jordan at 2026-02-26T00:47:12Z (change-id: chg-9927)

ryan_eng: thanks — can you attach the applied policy blob? asking because this smells like priority vs weight ordering + stickiness interaction.

devops_jordan: attaching the policy we deployed (snipped to relevant fields):

```
failover_policy:
  mode: weighted
  sticky_sessions: true
  targets:
    - region: us-west-2
      weight: 50
      priority: 2
    - region: eu-central-1
      weight: 50
      priority: 1
```

maria_support: ah — I think I see it. The intent was to prefer us-west-2 (priority 1) and fallback to eu (priority 2) but the priorities are reversed, plus sticky_sessions=true. That means existing sessions pinned to eu will stay there, and because priorities are flipped the routing algorithm will prefer eu.

ryan_eng: to expand: in `mode: weighted` the system first considers priorities (lower = higher preference). If a higher-priority target is available, weights are only used among targets with the same priority. Because eu has priority 1 the engine routes there. Sticky sessions then keep the client pinned to that region for subsequent requests which explains the persistent cross-region hits.

customer-sre: yikes. We never expected priority values to be inverted like that. Is there a safe rollback/patch we can do without a full restart?

maria_support: safest immediate fix is to flip the priority values so us-west-2 is 1 and eu is 2, and set sticky_sessions: false while we validate. Steps: 1) update policy -> dry-run 2) set sticky_sessions false 3) observe 5-10 minutes 4) re-enable stickiness if needed with correct priorities.

devops_jordan: applying change now (chg-9928):

```
failover_policy:
  mode: weighted
  sticky_sessions: false
  targets:
    - region: us-west-2
      weight: 70
      priority: 1
    - region: eu-central-1
      weight: 30
      priority: 2
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: updated failover-policy for org-12345 by devops_jordan at 2026-02-26T01:12:05Z (change-id: chg-9928)

ryan_eng: quick note — I increased us-west weight to 70 so that when priorities are equal (if someone later misconfigures them) default distribution still favors us-west. Also please confirm your client does not set any explicit region cookie. If your client sets the `rw_region` cookie it will override server-side sticky behavior.

customer-sre: we confirmed the cookie exists in older clients: `rw_region=eu-central-1; Path=/; Max-Age=86400` — looks like legacy behavior. We're rolling a client patch to stop setting that.

maria_support: good catch. For now with sticky_sessions=false the server will ignore existing rw_region cookies for routing. Monitor for ~30 minutes and let us know if you still see cross-region X-Served-Region headers.

(20m later) customer-sre: quick update — after the policy change and disabling stickiness the majority of requests are now served from us-west-2, p50 latency back to ~55ms. We still see ~2% to eu for clients with the cookie but it's diminishing as sessions expire. Billing spike normalized.

ryan_eng: great. Follow-ups: 1) we'll add a policy lint check in the console to flag priority/weight mismatches and warn against enabling sticky_sessions when priorities favor a different region. 2) we'll add a diagnostic endpoint that shows which routing rule matched for a request id. 3) ops: add a one-click rollback for recent policy changes for 15 minutes after deploy.

devops_jordan: thanks all — created ticket INF-487 to track the lint and rollback work.

customer-sre: thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

maria_support: marking this resolved, reopen if anything pops up.
